naslov: EuroLeague roundup: Hapoel rallies past Besiktas, Bayern upsets Efes, Virtus beats Paris
tekst:
By Eurohoops team/ info@eurohoops.net
Hapoel Tel Aviv secured a victory in the fifth round of the EuroLeague by defeating Besiktas 100-82 in a game played in Sofia.
After a balanced first half, during which Hapoel held a four-point lead (43-39), the decision came in the third quarter. At the very end of that quarter, the home team went on a 17-1 run, pulling away to a 75-55 lead, and maintained the difference easily until the end, reaching exactly 100 points with Amir Coffey’s basket in the final second.
Elijah Bryant and Vasilije Micic each scored 16 points, one more than Antonio Blakeney and Zach LeDay, while Amir Coffey, in his debut, had 12 points and seven rebounds.
On the other side, Ante Zizic had 17 points and nine rebounds, while Eugene Omoruyi added 12.
Bayern upsets Efes in Istanbul
Bayern pulled off a minor surprise in the fifth round of the EuroLeague by defeating Anadolu Efes 101-93 in Istanbul.
Evidently, Efes struggles without Mike James, which Bayern capitalized on to secure their second victory in the elite competition, leaving the Turkish team with just one win.
A crucial 8-0 run at the start of the final quarter allowed the visitors to pull ahead 85-72, and they secured the win without much drama.
Duane Washington scored 21 points, while Andreas Obst delivered his best performance of the season with 20 points and six assists. For the home team, Dario Saric scored 21 points and grabbed six rebounds, Cameron Payne had 18 points, Matthew Strazel contributed 15 points and seven assists, and Bruno Fernando recorded a double-double with 10 points and 12 rebounds.
Virtus wins a thriller against Paris
To close the round, Virtus Bologna secured a victory, edging out Paris on the road with a score of 96-94.
For the second round in a row, Paris had a shot to win but missed again. Last time it was Nadir Hifi, who was absent this game due to a wrist injury, and this time it was Tyson Etienne, who had seven three-pointers in the match.
After Marcus Carr made one free throw to give his team a 96-94 lead, the hosts had a full possession to win the game. However, Etienne missed, and Virtus secured their third victory, leaving Paris with just one win.
Derrick Alston Jr. scored 23 points, Wendell Moore added 14, Rasheed Bello 12, and Marcus Carr contributed 11 points along with six assists. For Paris, Etienne had 23 points and seven assists, while T.J. Warren added 19.

naslov: Zalgiris guard Carsen Edwards facing legal trouble in Kaunas
tekst:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net
Zalgiris guard Carsen Edwards is facing legal trouble after being pulled over by law enforcement in Kaunas following a domestic league victory.
As reported by Krepsinis.net on Monday, the 28-year-old American playmaker was caught driving under the influence of alcohol. The incident occurred during a late-night preventive police raid, just hours after his team’s game in Lithuania’s Betsson LKL against Lietkabelis on Sunday. Official police spokesperson Ramunas Matonis has confirmed the report, stating that the former NBA player registered a blood alcohol level of 1.07‰ while operating a Volkswagen Tiguan.
The offcourt situation overshadowed a strong performance in a winning effort for Zalgiris. Edwards played 17 minutes, contributing 11 points on perfect 4-of-4 shooting alongside six assists and an efficiency rating of 15 against Lietkabelis. Fueling a 4–0 domestic start, he has been a steady contributor, averaging 11.8 points over his first four LKL appearances.
The Houston native arrived in Lithuania this past summer. Tasked with replacing Sylvain Francisco, the veteran of 75 NBA games with the Boston Celtics and Detroit Pistons has started the continental schedule well. Through three EuroLeague games, the former 2024–25 All-EuroLeague First Team member is averaging 16.0 points, 2.0 assists, 1.0 rebounds, and 1.0 steals per contest.
The timing adds pressure to the team coached by Tomas Masiulis, which fell to 1–2 during a EuroLeague double-week with losses to Olympiacos and Paris. Zalgiris is currently preparing for a Round 4 matchup against FC Barcelona in Palau Blaugrana on Friday.
Zalgiris fines Edwards following the incident
Zalgiris announced that it has imposed a financial penalty on Edwards after reviewing the circumstances of the incident, in accordance with team rules. The club did not disclose the amount.
In its statement, Zalgiris said his conduct was inconsistent with the club’s values, the standards expected of professional athletes and the responsibilities of those representing the organization.
Edwards acknowledged his mistake, expressed sincere regret and accepted responsibility for his actions, according to the club. He also recognized the seriousness of the offense and that his behavior fell short of the required professional standards.
Zalgiris said it expects the incident to serve as an important lesson for Edwards, reiterating that everyone representing the club must respect the law and act responsibly both on and off the court.

naslov: Panathinaikos center Mathias Lessort picks up EuroLeague Round 4 MVP award
tekst:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net
Panathinaikos Aktor center Mathias Lessort has been officially named EuroLeague Round 4 Most Valuable Player for the 2026–27 Regular Season.
Euroleague Basketball confirmed the honor on Saturday.
Per the press release: “Mathias Lessort didn’t need long to make his mark in Round 4. The Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens center delivered a stellar performance in just 23 minutes to lead his team to a 92-75 home win over Fenerbahce Tarfin Istanbul and claim MVP of the Round honors with a PIR of 30.
Lessort scored 19 points on 6-of-9 two-point shooting and 7-of-10 from the free-throw line, adding 8 rebounds, an assist, a steal, a block and 6 fouls drawn. It is the fourth MVP of the Round award of his career, all with Panathinaikos, and his first since his fibula injury. His previous three came during the 2023-24 season.
Moses Wright of Armani Olimpia Milan posted the round’s highest PIR of 32, though it came in a 97-79 road loss to Maccabi Rapyd Tel Aviv. Wright had 23 points on 9-of-10 two-pointers and 5-of-6 free throws, plus 8 rebounds, an assist and 4 fouls drawn.
Chris Duarte followed with a PIR of 31 in Kosner Baskonia Vitoria-Gasteiz’s 84-92 home loss to Besiktas Istanbul. Duarte did most of his damage at the line, going a perfect 15-of-15 on free throws to finish with 23 points. He shot 1-of-3 on two-pointers and 2-of-4 from three-point range, and added 5 rebounds, an assist, 2 steals, a block and 7 fouls drawn.
Antonio Blakeney of Hapoel IBI Tel Aviv posted a PIR of 29 in a 93-82 road loss to Valencia Basket. He poured in 30 points on the back of 8-of-11 three-point shooting, adding 3-of-5 from inside the arc, 2 rebounds, 2 assists and a foul drawn.
Wendell Moore rounded out the top performers with a PIR of 28, contributing 20 points, 9 rebounds, 3 steals, a block and 5 fouls drawn as Virtus Bologna won 87-94 at FC Bayern Munich.
Individual highs: Nadir Hifi, Paris, 30 points
Hifi of Paris Basketball and Blakeney shared the round’s scoring lead with 30 points apiece. Hifi also tops the EuroLeague scoring charts at 20.3 points per game.
Kenneth Faried of Baskonia was the only player to reach double digits in rebounds, pulling down 10 against Besiktas. Elijah Bryant of Hapoel leads the league at 8.5 rebounds per game.
Devon Hall of Milan and Tomas Satoransky of Hapoel shared the assists lead with 9 each. Codi Miller-McIntyre of Olympiacos Piraeus leads the season standings at 6.7 assists per game.
Hifi also collected a round-high 4 steals in Paris’s 96-98 home loss to LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne. Luca Vildoza of Partizan leads the EuroLeague at 3.3 steals per game.
Austin Wiley of Bayern, Virtus teammates Aliou Diarra and Momo Diouf, and Dan Oturu of Hapoel each blocked 3 shots in Round 4. Jonas Valanciunas of Zalgiris Kaunas, Diarra and Oturu share the season lead at 2.3 blocks per game.
Faried’s 10 points and 10 rebounds against Besiktas made him the only player to record a double-double in Round 4.”

naslov: Olympiacos excludes Dorsey from game vs Barcelona
tekst:
By Stefan Acevski / info@eurohoops.net
Tyler Dorsey heard what Chima Moneke and Jaron Blossomgame said on the “Triple Threat Show” podcast about his role at Olympiacos, in relation to a possible contract extension and when Olympiacos should offer it—and he did not leave their comments unanswered.
Chima Moneke described Dorsey as essential, while Jaron Blossomgame considered him expendable.
At that point, Dorsey picked up his phone and replied to Blossomgame and also to the show co-host Dionysis Aravantinos:
“Jaron Blossomgame, if everything I do is replaceable, why don’t you just go ahead and let me go now, especially if they don’t want to pay me. Why waste time and drama? Why does the coaching staff have that fear in their heart? Let’s find out!”
“Dionysis Aravantinos, my minutes went down out of nowhere. But no need for me to drop everything now. The truth will be told about how I been done over here; not everything what it seems like from afar!”
After his quotes, Olympiacos announced that Tyler Dorsey has been left out of the squad for the match against Barcelona and will return to Athens immediately.
Dorsey is in the final year of his contract with Olympiacos, and so far there is no progress on a possible extension.

naslov: Barcelona and Bayern not expected to attend meeting for NBA Europe, Madrid in contact
tekst:
By Aris Barkas/ barkas@eurohoops.net
A crucial week is ahead for the NBA Europe project, according to reports from across Europe and information from Eurohoops sources.
As Sky Sports reported, a meeting is expected in London, where the Ballon d’Or ceremony will be held on Monday.
According to the British report, PSG, Bayern Munich, AC Milan, Barcelona and Real Madrid are expected to be attend, but Catalan newspaper “Sport” reveals that Barcelona and Bayern will not be part of the meeting.
Various sources have confirmed to EuroLeague that Barcelona and Bayern are keeping a firm stance, aligned with the decision taken in Como by the EuroLeague owners; on the other hand, Real Madrid seems to be the EuroLeague club more inclined to continue a dialogue with the NBA.
The numbers of the offer
The negative stance of the EuroLeague clubs can be explained by the numbers presented by “Sport”.
According to the report, the total offer to the EuroLeague shareholders was 520M euros to abolish the league and join the new project; This makes it 40M per club, and they would also lose ownership of the league.
On top of that, they also had to pay 400M euros each as a participation fee. Essentially, the EuroLeague clubs got only a discount on the minimum half-million bid that the NBA has set for participation in the new league, which means that, in theory, they need 40 M in revenue annually per club for the next decade, just to recover the participation fee.

naslov: Richard Deitz moves to legal action for Maccabi ownership and responds to Shimon Mizrahi
tekst:
By Aris Barkas/ barkas@eurohoops.net
The new owner of Maccabi may be decided in the Tel Aviv District Court via arbitration.
Minority shareholder Richard Deitz, who used his right of first refusal to become the majority owner of Maccabi, responded with legal action to Maccabi chairman Shimon Mizrahi’s countermove.
Mizrahi used his own right of first refusal to get the majority, and the result might be an arbitration, with Deitz not wanting the majority of the ownership to be transferred to US-based businessman Jason Levien.
Deitz made the following announcement in which he explains his action and also responds to Shimon Mizrahi: “Today, as reported in the press, I filed a motion for urgent relief with the Economic Division of the Tel Aviv District Court and a notice of arbitration. I took this step reluctantly after Oudi Recanati sent a midnight notice canceling a planned shareholder meeting and announcing the unilateral transfer of 7.5% of the shares of Maccabi to Jason Levien. This transfer, in contradiction to the requirements of the shareholder agreement, was the latest in a series of violations which have grown too numerous to count. All of these violations were contrived to conceal attempts to transfer control of the club to Jason Levien.
I also read Shimon Mizrahi’s statement yesterday. Shimon is a legend, and I have tremendous respect for him. Maccabi’s trophy case is full of hardware won under his long stewardship. Maccabi has been his life’s work and his love for the club is unquestioned. This is a love we both share, even if we differ in our vision.
Where I part from Shimon is in slandering one’s partners. To deceive and plot against a partner and then call that partner disloyal for placing his allegiance with Maccabi rather than the plotters is hypocritical. All the more so when that partner has, for 13 years, steadfastly supported the club, never made waves or sought publicity, and always worked to heal the rifts between partners and build consensus.
I’m aware of the intense interest among our fan base in this matter. It’s because all of you are stakeholders in Maccabi. It is also regrettable. We are on the verge of a new season, which we approach with hope and high expectations. This internal battle does not put Maccabi’s ownership in a good light and is a distraction. It will also take time to play out.
I don’t believe in litigating in public. There is much dirty laundry to be aired, but legal matters are for courts and arbitrators to decide, having reference to facts, documents, and the law. I know our fans and the media will follow this story, but I want to remind everyone that the more important story is the one on the court. Oded and our Captain, John D., will be leading our squad into battle with an exciting roster. Regardless of your point of view, I ask you to give the team your full support.
In the fullness of time, the ownership issues will be resolved. Perhaps at some point cooler heads and rationality might even prevail. But regardless of those divisions, there should be no daylight between any of us when it comes to supporting our team.
Yalla Maccabi!”

naslov: Panathinaikos officially asked EuroLeague to open a disciplinary proceeding vs. coach Bartzokas
tekst:
By Stefan Acevski / info@eurohoops.net
Dimitris Giannakopoulos posted a series of stories on his personal Instagram account, referring to the events that took place yesterday in Bologna, immediately after Marcus Carr’s winning shot.
Olympiacos reacted with a tweet on the club account, and Panathinaikos made an official demand to EuroLeague to open a disciplinary proceeding.
The owner of Panathinaikos called for an investigation to be opened, referring to Bartzokas’s push to Virtus players who were moving towards him while celebrating.
Giannakopoulos said: “When I see such actions—people tarnishing a product that the EuroLeague has done a good job developing over the past few years, increasing its value and so on—and these actions go unpunished, unlike those involving team officials, myself included, I find it difficult to understand. Players receive fines ranging from tens to hundreds of thousands of euros for saying something about a referee. Yet there is physical violence, and not even an investigation is opened? I simply don’t understand it. 
Either we protect the product, or we don’t. It is not right that I receive a three-game suspension, even during the Final Four, for standing three meters behind the scorer’s table, while coaches, players, officials, or anyone else can engage in physical violence without anyone touching them and remain above the law. Enough is enough.”
Earlier, Giannakopoulos had shared another post stating: “Ten months and a €2 million fine for Giannakopoulos,” accompanying it with a video from the end of Olympiacos’ game in Bologna.
The footage showed the moment after Marcus Carr’s buzzer-beating three-pointer, when Virtus Bologna’s players celebrated in front of the Olympiacos coach.
As for the official complaint, Panathinaikos is demanding an exemplary punishment for the Olympiacos coach, citing his “repeated inappropriate behaviors over the years”, which they claim have been an absolute discredit to the sport and the EuroLeague product. They highlighted his “outrageous actions after last year’s away game against Dubai, where he attacked fans in the stands, insulted a female fan, his similar behavior at the Final Four in Abu Dhabi, and many other incidents”.
According to Panathinaikos, Bartzokas “should not be allowed to continue discrediting the sport with impunity while other sports officials are rightfully punished for their actions”.
Olympiacos’ response
After Giannakopoulos’ stories, Olympiacos BC, through their account on X, made their stance clear, specifically stating: “It’s pain, IT WON’T pass!”
It’s probably an innuendo for Olympiacos winning the EuroLeague title last season on Panathinaikos home court.

naslov: Fenerbahce beats Dubai in the EuroLeague SuperCup third-place game
tekst:
By Eurohoops team/ info@eurohoops.net
Fenerbahce is leaving Abu Dhabi on a high note after beating Dubai BC in the third-place game of the first ever EuroLeague SuperCup.
The final score was 85-77 with Wade Baldwin scoring all of his 11 points in the fourth quarter and deciding the game. Still,  Talen Horton-Tucker carried the team with 23 points, while newcomer Trent Forrest also added 11 points.
Elie Okobo and Davis Bertans with 14 points each led Dubai, which couldn’t recover after a crucial 10-0 run by Fenerbahce, which gave the eventual winners a 74-70 lead.
“I think we played well in three of the four quarters”, said Fenerbahce coach Sarunas Jasikevicius after the final buzzer.
As he explained: “We were good in the first two quarters, but then we weren’t prepared for the physicality Dubai brought to the game in the third quarter; they tried to turn the match around using that physicality. We showed both good and bad sides of ourselves during this SuperCup”.
“Yes, it’s true that we have a talented roster, however, talent isn’t what will determine the kind of season we have”, Saras added, “there are so many small details—physicality, loose balls… It is details like these that will define our season.”

naslov: Real Madrid director backs NBA expansion to Europe: “The sooner, the better”
tekst:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net
Real Madrid basketball director Juan Carlos Sanchez wants the NBA to expand into Europe, stating that a partnership between the two entities should happen ‘the sooner, the better’.
Speaking on Realmadrid TV on Monday, the 65-year-old executive confirmed an upcoming meeting in Italy, where Euroleague Basketball owners will gather to discuss an active proposal from the league based in North America.
“We are eager for the NBA to come to Europe,” said Sanchez. “The NBA is the premier league in the world and would give basketball on the continent a massive leap, economically, in media exposure, and in overall presence.”
“It is like being offered a Ferrari for the weekend,” added the Madrid native. “The NBA in Europe would be incredibly important for every club. Hopefully, the sooner, the better. But right now, we have to play in the Liga Endesa and the EuroLeague, trying to win every title possible. If the NBA does come later, the first championship ring is for Madrid.”
Addressing financial regulations
Sanchez also discussed other topics, including budget rises across EuroLeague team. To control this inflation, the Madrid executive believes Europe needs to adopt American-style financial restrictions.
“With the NBA, that would have limits,” he mentioned. “A salary cap has to be on the table. In the NBA, if you spend too much, you pay a fine that gets distributed to other teams, so you end up helping your competitors. The NBA regulates the sport well. It has the draft. It has experience with these things. In Europe, we perhaps act as a talent laboratory. We focus on individual and team technique, producing great players. But when it comes to commercial structure and the business side of things, the NBA has it very well organized.”

naslov: Olympiacos has filed two formal complaints against Giannakopoulos and PAO
tekst:
By Aris Barkas/ barkas@eurohoops.net
In the aftermath of all six suspects in the Greek basketball scandal testifying and hearing the charges against them, Olympiacos officially announced that the club has filed two formal complaints, both in the EuroLeague and the Greek League, against Panathinaikos and club owner Dimitris Giannakopoulos.
The complaints concern both the offensive conduct of Panathinaikos fans during the EuroLeague game against Baskonia and the social media posts made by Giannakopoulos on his personal Instagram account.
In the case of the EuroLeague complaint, the chants from Panathinaikos fans and a banner held during the game, which were reposted on social media by Giannakopoulos, are, according to Olympiacos, “manifestly defamatory, insulting and discrediting towards our club and our coach, Mr. Giorgos Bartzokas.”
In the case of the Greek League complaint, four social media posts are mentioned which present “as a fact something absolutely false and slanderous, that our team is allegedly a participant or accomplice in the criminal offenses for which referee Vaso Tsarouha is accused, i.e. in the manipulation of basketball matches and that our team has been favored or benefited from the commission of said alleged offences.”
Dimitris Giannakopoulos already commented on the complaints, again on his social media, saying that Olympiacos management is “incapable of learning.”

naslov: Real Madrid falls in Pedro Martinez’s preseason debut, Bayern starts with a win
tekst:
By Eurohoops team/ info@eurohoops.net
Pedro Martinez’s tenure as Real Madrid head coach began with a 110-102 preseason defeat to Rio Breogan in Pontevedra.
Madrid remained competitive until the closing stages, but their lack of rhythm and conditioning became increasingly evident. The EuroLeague side was without Facundo Campazzo, Gabriel Deck, Andres Feliz, Jaime Pradilla, Max Shulga, Mikael Jantunen and Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot.
With limited options available, Martinez used a short rotation. Theo Maledon and Gabriele Procida were aggressive from the start, while Olivier Sarr also produced several positive plays. However, Breogan imposed its physicality and led 26-22 after the opening quarter.
Walter Tavares made his return following a serious knee injury and provided some productive minutes, but Breogan continued to find success from three-point range and in transition to take a 51-46 halftime lead.

Stephen Curry has secured a contract extension with the Golden State Warriors, confirming projections on the final chapters of his historic NBA career.

The Warriors later annouced the agreement and released further details on Friday.

“We couldn’t be more excited about reaching an agreement with Stephen and extending his historic career with the Warriors,” said Warriors General Manager Mike Dunleavy. “Personally, I don’t think there has ever been a better face to a franchise in professional sports history, both on and off the court, than Stephen Curry with the Warriors. He embodies everything this organization strives to represent through his legendary play on the court, his unique leadership and sacrifice, and his unmatched impact in the community. We’ve been incredibly blessed to experience 17 years of Stephen’s artistry and are thrilled that our fans will continue to have the opportunity to watch him perform and write additional chapters to his illustrious story.”
Curry, 38, averaged 26.6 points, 4.7 assists, 3.6 rebounds and 1.1 steals in 30.9 minutes per game across 43 games (41 starts) in 2025-26, earning his 12th career NBA All-Star selection. Curry missed 39 games in 2025-26, including 27 due to patellofemoral pain syndrome, or bone bruising, in his right knee.

A member of the NBA’s 75th Anniversary Team and 11-time All-NBA Team selection, Curry is the NBA’s all-time 3-point leader with 4,248 career regular-season threes (42.2 3P%) and holds the all-time playoff record with 650 3-pointers on 39.7% shooting. He also holds the NBA’s highest all-time regular-season free throw percentage, shooting 91.2% on 4,645 career attempts. Curry ranks as the franchise’s all-time leader in points (26,528), field goals (9,022), assists (6,743), steals (1,602) and games played (1,069). The 2022 NBA Finals MVP has helped lead the Warriors to four NBA championships (2015, 2017, 2018, 2022), six NBA Finals appearances (2015-19, 2022), 10 playoff berths (2013-2019, 2022-23, 2024-25) and an NBA-record 73-win season in 2015-16. He earned back-to-back MVP Awards in 2014-15 and 2015-16 and is the only player ever to win the award by a unanimous vote (2015-16).
Internationally, Curry earned his first Olympic gold medal with Team USA at the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris, averaging a team-best 14.8 points, 3.2 rebounds and 2.5 assists in 23.3 minutes in six games. He joined LeBron James, Magic Johnson, Michael Jordan and Bill Russell as the only players in NBA history to win at least four NBA championships, two MVP Awards and an Olympic gold medal.”

Guerschon Yabusele sees a connection between Panathinaikos and the Boston Celtics that goes beyond their shared colors.

“I wanted to play for the best coach in the EuroLeague and alongside some of the best players. I wanted to join a top-level team that wants to be at the very top.”
